title: Aaron Rodgers secretly funded his town's Flock-style cameras
excerpt: The QB loves privacy. Except when it comes to other people.
content_html:
Hello there!

I’m here much earlier than normal today. I hope you don’t mind. My apologies if I’ve completely thrown off your circadian reading rhythm.

That’s enough preamble. Let’s begin.

Aaron Rodgers cares about privacy. A lot. 

The star quarterback has repeatedly spoken out about our current culture's flagrant disregard for people’s desire to avoid prying eyes.  

"It's a sick society, isn't it?” Rodgers said in a June 2025 appearance on The Pat McAfee Show. “What is [it with] the entitlement to information that we're living in society these days?”

Months later, Rodgers bemoaned that he was under constant, technologically supercharged surveillance, claiming that paparazzi had been “flying drones over my house.”

It got so bad, he said, that he left his longtime Malibu home. 

I get why Rodgers is upset. It is a sick society, isn’t it? We live in a world now where people can suddenly subject anyone to invasive, omnipresent monitoring, entirely without their consent. 

Like this one small town in New Jersey, where local cops recently added new tools to their surveillance arsenal. Unbeknownst to the people who live there, the effort was the work of a single wealthy individual. A recent transplant to the town, they funded the police department’s purchase of a number of Flock-style license plate cameras.

This person used an LLC as a cutout to shield their identity, secretly helping enhance a digital dragnet that robs residents of their right to privacy. 

I have to assume Aaron Rodgers doesn’t have an issue with that, though.

After all, he’s the one who did it. 

But if you’re not ready to pull out your credit card just yet, we offer big stories for free every single Thursday.

content_html_zh:
你好呀！

我今天比平时早到了。 我希望你不介意。 如果我完全打乱了你的昼夜阅读节奏，我深表歉意。

序言已经足够了。 让我们开始吧。

亚伦·罗杰斯关心隐私。 很多。

这位明星四分卫多次公开表示，我们当前的文化公然无视人们避免窥探的愿望。

“这是一个病态的社会，不是吗？” 罗杰斯于 2025 年 6 月在帕特·迈克菲秀上露面时说道。 “我们现在生活在社会中，获得信息的权利是什么？”

几个月后，罗杰斯哀叹自己一直受到技术上超强的监视，声称狗仔队“用无人机飞过我的房子”。

他说，情况变得如此糟糕，以至于他离开了他在马里布长期居住的家。

我明白罗杰斯为什么不高兴。 这是一个病态的社会，不是吗？ 我们现在生活在一个人们可以突然对任何人进行侵入性、无所不在的监控的世界，完全不需要他们的同意。

就像新泽西州的这个小镇一样，当地警察最近在他们的监控武器库中添加了新工具。 住在那里的人们不知道的是，这项工作是由一个富有的人完成的。 他们最近搬到了该镇，资助警察局购买了一些 Flock 式车牌摄像头。

此人利用有限责任公司作为保护自己身份的切口，暗中帮助增强了剥夺居民隐私权的数字天罗地网。

不过，我必须假设亚伦·罗杰斯对此没有意见。

毕竟，他是做这件事的人。
